To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The Standard Model (SM) light Higgs scenario is excluded by the current data at 99% confidence level, and (ii) the infinite Higgs mass limit of composite Higgs theories is not excluded by the current LHC data at 99.7% confidence level.
the Higgs boson mass is a crucial parameter for the determination of a composite Higgs model signal, and that the Higgs mass range of interest for a composite Higgs scenario is 120-140 GeV.
the Higgs boson mass is not a fundamental parameter of the Standard Model and can be predicted by its own decay rate in the infinite Higgs mass limit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Higgs sector in composite Higgs models and in the Standard Model, in the context of ℓν + 4 jets production at the 7 and 14 TeV LHC.
the study of the Higgs boson in the light of the new physics scenarios.
a complete parton level study of lν + 4 jets production at the 7 TeV LHC.
